content.thinking:
I'll answer this as a concrete Android engineering question: how to give a launcher icon that degrades gracefully for API 24 and 25 while keeping a proper adaptive icon for API 26 and above. The angle I'll take is the resource-qualifier one, because that's where the question actually lives. A density-independent folder named mipmap with no qualifier is valid, so the plan is to keep the adaptive XML in mipmap-anydpi-v26 and add a plain vector at res/mipmap/ic_launcher.xml that the build resolves below API 26. I'll also note that AAPT wants a default resource so a manifest pointing only at the v26 folder with minSdk 24 would fail to build, and I'll explain that a VectorDrawable used as a launcher icon works on API 24 and 25 because the package manager loads it through Resources.getDrawable.

From there I'll lay out the app itself, since the notes cover a full implementation. Package com.example.snake, three source files plus one layout-free view. I'll describe a pure-logic engine class holding the grid, an ArrayDeque of packed cell indices with the head first, a small queue of pending directions capped at two so illegal reversals get dropped, score, tick count, and an alive flag. A step function returns whether the snake moved, ate, or died, checking wall bounds and body overlap while allowing entry into the tail cell when not growing. Speed will be derived from score and elapsed ticks, clamped between a floor and a ceiling.

Then the rendering side: a custom View that computes a cell size from the measured dimensions, floors it, centers the board with letterboxing, and lays out a HUD band above. Dark background, faint grid lines, gradient snake segments as rounded rectangles, eyes oriented by direction, a pulsing apple, score and best in the HUD, and an overlay panel for game over with a new-best line. Input via a swipe threshold on move with taps reserved for pause, resume, and restart, plus haptic feedback on eating. A frame loop driven by postOnAnimation accumulating nanoseconds so speed changes apply smoothly, paused and resumed from the activity lifecycle, best score persisted in shared preferences.

I'll close by confirming the fallback icon approach is the right one and that the vector-in-mipmap default resolves cleanly for API 24 and 25 while the adaptive icon still takes over on 26+.

content.text:
Build succeeded — `app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`.

**What's in it**

Kotlin, single module (`app`), package `com.example.snake`, **zero third-party dependencies** — plain `android.app.Activity` plus a custom `View`, so nothing to resolve beyond the Kotlin/AGP plugins themselves.

- **`SnakeGame.kt`** — pure logic, no Android imports. Body is an `ArrayDeque<Int>` of cells packed as `y*cols + x`; a 16×28 grid. Two-slot turn buffer so a quick double swipe isn't dropped, opposite-direction reversals rejected, and the tail cell counts as free on a non-growing step (standard Snake forgiveness).
- **`GameView.kt`** — renders and drives the loop. Cell size is computed to fit the board area, centered under a HUD band; checkerboard tiles, gradient body from head to tail, eyes that rotate with direction, pulsing apple with stalk and leaf, expanding ring on eat plus haptic tick.
- **`MainActivity.kt`** — hosts the view, immersive fullscreen on both the API 30+ and legacy paths, keeps the screen on, and pauses on `onPause`.

**Requirements covered**

| Requirement | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Swipe controls | 22dp slop threshold; direction picked from the dominant axis; swipe also resumes/starts |
| Score | HUD counter, best score persisted in `SharedPreferences` |
| Game over + restart | Overlay panel with score, best, "NEW BEST!" flag and tap-to-replay |
| Speed increases over time | Step interval drops with both score (7ms/fruit) and elapsed ticks (1.5ms/tick), floor 70ms; ten-dot speed meter in the HUD |

Two snags during the build: Kotlin's `ArrayDeque` has no `pollFirst` (used `removeFirst` guarded by the fill queue), and the overlay `when` needed a `RUNNING` branch. The only remaining output is a deprecation warning for `setDecorFitsSystemWindows`.

Install with `adb install -r app\build\outputs\apk\debug\app-debug.apk`.
